subroutine tirust_finalize(status)
    integer, intent(out), optional :: status
    integer :: result
    local_error = ''
    result = destroy_context(context)
    if (result == TIRUST_SUCCESS) context = c_null_ptr
    if (present(status)) status = result
  end subroutine

  subroutine tirust_clear_cache(status)
    integer, intent(out), optional :: status
    integer :: result
    call ensure_context(result)
    if (result == TIRUST_SUCCESS) result = clear_cache(context)
    if (present(status)) status = result
  end subroutine

subroutine tensor_mp(n,rank,shifts,invariants,masses,mu2,coefs,status, &
                       pole_mode,compute_finite,check_pass,cache_enabled)
    integer, intent(in) :: n,rank
    real(KI_QTIR), intent(in) :: shifts(0:,:),invariants(:,:),mu2
    complex(KI_QTIR), intent(in) :: masses(:)
    complex(KI_QTIR), intent(out) :: coefs(:,:)
    integer, intent(out) :: status
    integer, intent(in), optional :: pole_mode
    logical, intent(in), optional :: compute_finite,check_pass,cache_enabled
    integer(c_int) :: poles,finite,check,cache
    character(kind=c_char), allocatable :: p_text(:,:),s_text(:,:),m_text(:,:),output(:,:)
    character(kind=c_char) :: scale_text(record_size)
    real(KI_QTIR), allocatable :: values(:)
    integer :: i,j,k,count,ios
    coefs = cmplx(0,0,kind=KI_QTIR)
    if (.not.valid_shapes(n,rank,shape(shifts),shape(invariants),size(masses),shape(coefs),status)) return
    status = TIRUST_UNSUPPORTED
    local_error = 'TIRust quadruple precision requires a binary128 kind with 113 significand bits.'
    if (radix(mu2) /= 2 .or. digits(mu2) /= 113) return
    count = tirust_coefficient_count(rank)
    status = TIRUST_ERROR
    local_error = 'TIRust quadruple-precision transport allocation failed.'
    if (int(count,c_int64_t)*8_c_int64_t > int(huge(count),c_int64_t)) return
    allocate(p_text(record_size,4*n),s_text(record_size,n*n),m_text(record_size,2*n), &
             output(record_size,8*count),values(8*count),stat=ios)
    if (ios /= 0) return
    local_error = 'TIRust could not encode a finite binary128 input.'
    do i=1,n
      call pack(real(masses(i),kind=KI_QTIR),m_text(:,2*i-1),ios)
      if (ios /= 0) return
      call pack(aimag(masses(i)),m_text(:,2*i),ios)
      if (ios /= 0) return
      do j=0,3
        call pack(shifts(j,i),p_text(:,4*(i-1)+j+1),ios)
        if (ios /= 0) return
      enddo
      do j=1,n
        call pack(invariants(j,i),s_text(:,n*(i-1)+j),ios)
        if (ios /= 0) return
      enddo
    enddo
    call pack(mu2,scale_text,ios)
    if (ios /= 0) return
    call options(pole_mode,compute_finite,check_pass,cache_enabled,poles,finite,check,cache)
    call ensure_context(status)
    if (status /= TIRUST_SUCCESS) return
    status = evaluate_mp(context,int(n,c_int),int(rank,c_int),p_text,size(p_text,kind=c_size_t), &
                         s_text,size(s_text,kind=c_size_t),m_text,size(m_text,kind=c_size_t), &
                         scale_text,size(scale_text,kind=c_size_t),output,size(output,kind=c_size_t), &
                         poles,finite,check,cache)
    if (status /= TIRUST_SUCCESS) return
    do k=1,8*count
      call unpack(output(:,k),values(k),ios)
      if (ios /= 0) then
        ! Native insertion precedes this public Fortran transport check.
        ! Reject all numerical cache entries when decoding the result fails.
        ios = clear_cache(context)
        status = TIRUST_ERROR
        local_error = 'TIRust returned an invalid or nonfinite binary128 output record.'
        return
      endif
    enddo
    do j=1,4
      do i=1,count
        k = 2*((j-1)*count+i)
        coefs(i,j) = cmplx(values(k-1),values(k),kind=KI_QTIR)
      enddo
    enddo
  end subroutine

# Private partial-DD prototype proposal

This source-only proposal enables one existing option in the finite-DP
embedded workspace: `partial_rescue=true`. The control arm keeps it false.
`arms.patch` is exactly that one-line difference. Both arms have identical
private integer-only telemetry; neither changes a production source, installed
library, generated Fortran, card, input point, normalization or host policy.
No dependency tree has been copied, compiler invoked, library loaded or test
executed. Source derivation is the only operation performed here.

The motivation is the frozen `qcd-dp-policy-audit` (`196e8b59…`): 102 final
refused visits are non-top box subsets in N5/rank4 calls, whereas 32 top-box
visits are excluded. Eight of the 13 rescued points contain both. At most five
points lack that recorded exclusion; this is not a prediction of DD success,
remaining recurrence success, host acceptance, saved QP calls or elapsed time.

## Numerical change and exclusions

`bridge-partial.patch` derives from the installed scientific Rust source
`455529b9…`. The only numerical change from the identically instrumented
control is the default option override. The existing core still decides
eligibility: binary64, non-top PV triangle/box, no jet/dimension shift,
nonzero Gram solve and failed conditioning. Its DD gate remains `2^-66`.
No top-box, bubble, exact-singular, master-error or invalid-input retry is
added. Gram-method choice retains precedence in its own pass. Whole-lane
precision tiers remain disabled. All original direct/method-choice thresholds,
master kernels, variant rules and rounding are untouched.

Fortran supplies the same 53-bit values; eligible subsets lift those exact
values into DoubleFloat, compute their existing DD recurrence and round its
coefficients into the remaining DP recurrence. This is **embedded partial DD**,
not genuine QP. The genuine 113-bit-input QP path remains unchanged. Pole-only
DP/QP and finite QP code are unchanged. Immutable plans stay shared; mutable
primary/check workspaces stay separate. No numerical store is attached to a
check. Existing partial-rescue keys include threshold/input precision;
ordinary shared-subset keys include partial configuration. Control and
candidate use separate processes/contexts and must never share numerical
stores. Failure still clears the store and destroys both directional
workspaces. Cache budgets, event clearing and finalize behavior are unchanged.

## Actual work observation

The private core patch inserts fixed-size integer counters at existing branch
and call boundaries; it does not inspect unsuccessful coefficient buffers,
change FP flags or rounding, evaluate a helper integral, allocate trace strings
or perform I/O. A thread-local `Cell<[u64;11]>` is reset at entry to the
serialized `State::dp_checked`. The same state copies it after the complete
result/finiteness/failure-invalidation path, including returned errors, and
keeps cumulative and last-call arrays. No callback or unsafe code enters the
core. The safe core's `forbid(unsafe_code)` stays intact.

The counters distinguish geometric selections from **actual DD evaluator
starts**, success/refusal/Rust errors, successful/failed partial-subset cache
lookups, and complete injection-function success/failure. Selections can occur
before a later geometry failure prevents evaluation; they must not be called
DD attempts. A successful numerical DD status can precede an injection-layout
or later parent failure; neither is an accepted tensor/amplitude. Counts can
include multiple variant attempts and repeated subset visits. A pipeline
failure includes preparation/layout errors; it is not relabeled a numerical
DD refusal. Counter overflow is explicit and disqualifies quantitative use.

The new private 30-word C getter is specified in `telemetry.h`. It reads context
state only. Sequence/N/rank/mode/status identify the last completed DP call;
prevalidation rejection leaves the old sequence, and poisoned contexts remain
errors. Getter calls have the existing guard's last-error clearing behavior:
an observer must copy native error and entry/exit IEEE state **before** reading
telemetry. No clear or statistics call resets cumulative counts; context
destruction does. Fixed synchronous calling-thread ownership is required.
This observer has not yet passed compiled or IEEE parity qualification.

Public status `219` remains the DP-interface result. The diagnostic record
must identify the candidate as `partial-DD-enabled`, retain exact observed
attempt/success/cache counters, and never label such a call pure DP merely
because its last counters are zero: ordinary cached intermediates may have
earlier DD ancestry. A successful final amplitude is not certified by a
successful subset. The independent MadLoop reversal/rotation and explicit
genuine-QP fallback remain responsible for acceptance.

# Static audit of higher-multiplicity cache reuse

This is a source-only audit, with no implementation, native execution or new
performance measurement. No active numerical values, cards or filters were
read. The closed 76-call lifecycle proof covers native-DP real-SM processes
through N=3/rank=2; its QP requests are explicit tensor diagnostics. It does
not exercise physical QP rescues, repeated DP failures or cache saturation.

## What is already reused

Automatic event entry/exit and Lorentz rotations clear numerical caches
(`loop_matrix_standalone.inc:954–957,993–997,2046–2073`). There is no unconditional
native clear inside the helicity or split-order loops. Immutable plans and
structural workspaces survive ordinary native clears (`lib.rs:644–654`).
Generated plan registration is unique by `(N,rank)` and skipped after a
subprocess's context generation is registered (`loop_exporters.py:2680–2687`,
`TIRUST_interface.inc:325–334`). Context destruction changes the generation.

Born interference normally accumulates numerator coefficients over helicities
before reducing, then loops over split orders (`loop_matrix_standalone.inc:
1118–1319,1391–1402`). Amplitude reduction, including loop-induced processes,
reduces inside the helicity loop instead (1198–1209). Consequently, many
helicities do not automatically imply repeated native integrals in Born mode.

| Path | Reuse and independent-check behavior |
|---|---|
| DP host tensor cache | Enabled for amplitude reduction or multiple squared split orders; keys are loop group and CT-mode slot, independent of numerator/helicity. Hits bypass the TIRust adapter. |
| Full DP native | Shared subintegral store on primary passes; independent checks attach no numerical store. Two structural workspaces per `(N,rank)`, distinguished by check flag. |
| Pole DP native | Separate pole store on primary passes; checks attach no numerical store. Primary/check share a structural workspace per `(N,rank)`. |
| QP native | Exact decimal-request whole-tensor cache on primary passes; checks bypass it. No MPFR subintegral sharing. Full/poles keys are distinct; each precision path retains a structural workspace per `(N,rank)`. |

These paths are defined in `TIR_interface.inc:237–328`,
`helas_loop_amplitude.inc:174–180,213–219` and `lib.rs:91–118,162–268,337–348`.
QP calls bypass the DP host tensor cache and still perform Fortran kinematic
preparation and decimal transport, including on a native exact-request hit.

## Findings that need measurement

1. **Failure invalidation can discard successful work elsewhere in the event.**
   Any full-DP non-success clears the entire shared DP store and drops both
   directional workspaces for the failing `(N,rank)` (`lib.rs:128–160`). This
   also happens after a failed check or cache-disabled call, although that call
   attached no shared store. Earlier successful topologies lose their native
   entries; their immutable plans remain. The store clear resets counters as
   well as entries (pinned TIRust `direct/shared.rs:509–535`), so a final snapshot
   can conceal the discarded work. This is conservative correctness protection,
   not an established defect. Do not remove it without a proof that failed
   intermediate entries cannot survive. The small lifecycle proof has no
   physical failure cascade.

2. **The native budget is partitioned without borrowing.** With pole support,
   the default 256 MiB becomes 64 MiB full DP, 64 MiB pole DP and 128 MiB QP
   (`lib.rs:59–76,279–284`). Full DP cannot use an idle pole/QP share. The limits
   account for numerical entries, not all plans, geometry variants, workspaces
   and transport buffers. No saturation or memory-pressure conclusion follows
   from this source fact.

3. **Native cache0 does not disable the DP host tensor cache.**
   `TIRustGlobalCache` supplies the native cache flag
   (`TIRUST_interface.inc:106–108,232–234`); the host cache does not consult it.
   `TIRCaching` is independently enabled by `loop_exporters.py:884–889`.
   Therefore a cache0/−1 comparison for loop-induced or mixed-order processes
   can retain host tensor hits in both arms. Single-split-order Born processes
   have no such host tensor cache. This distinction must appear in profiling
   labels and hit counts.

4. **Unselected backends still perform empty TIRust lifecycle work.**
   Whenever TIRust was available at export, `CLEAR_CACHES` calls its clear even
   if backend9 is never selected (2064–2066). `mtirust.f90:137–142` ensures a
   context before clearing, so a first event can create an otherwise unused
   context; later event entry/exit calls still cross the FFI and mutex.
   A null-context fast return would change generation/error observability and
   is not implemented here. Measure this separately in explicit1/6/7/8 lanes.

Other source-visible costs worth separating in that profile are repeated
kinematic construction, same-store attachment/registration, QP key allocation
and full-answer copying, and QP/pole geometry changes between directions.
For example, N=6/rank=6 has 210 coefficients: the four-slot QP answer is
107,520 ASCII bytes. Its Fortran transport allocation payload is 139,008 bytes
per call before allocator overhead (`mtirust.f90:319–320`), including hits.
These are dimensional calculations, not observed allocations or time costs.

## Gram normalization: a signed-zero-only proposal is defensible

The checked-worker site at ELF `0x11fcecb` is in `gram_indicator::<f64>`.
Retained `gram.rs:724–725` computes
`w = largest / sqrt(cnorm2(delta).to_f64())`, then returns
`(largest > 0.0 && w.is_finite()).then_some(w)`.
The resulting `Option` is consumed by `alternative_estimate_of` at lines
963–965 to select a reduction estimate; it is not a disposable diagnostic.

`gram-zero-only.patch` proposes computing the same denominator, then checking
its integer bits for **either signed zero**, returning `None` only in that
case. For all nonzero bit patterns, leave the old division and predicate
unchanged. All determinant, numerator, conversion and square-root arithmetic
preceding the division remains in place.

The old masked `Option` value is provably `None` for a zero denominator:

| Numerator | Masked division by either signed zero | Old returned value |
|---|---|---|
| Nonzero finite value or infinity | Infinity, with sign determined by operands | `None` |
| Either signed zero | NaN | `None` |
| Any NaN | NaN | `None` |

This covers the returned variant across rounding modes. It does not promise
identical discarded NaN payloads or uninitialized `Option` representation bytes.
The integer test adds no floating comparison of a signaling NaN. Do not broaden
the guard to reject nonfinite denominators: a positive finite `largest` divided
by positive infinity currently produces `Some(+0)`. Nonfinite and nonzero
values retain their old path under this proposal.

This **intentionally changes exception flags and trap execution** on the
selected branch; it is not full IEEE equivalence. Earlier arithmetic can still
trap. A tiny nonzero denominator can still overflow the division, so this guard
is not established as a remedy for the observed failure. Rust/LLVM code
generation must also be inspected: a source-level control guard alone is not
proof that an exceptional operation will not be speculated in a new binary.

Before any promotion, root must approve a new isolated build and validate
signed zeros, zero/nonzero/infinite/NaN numerators, all nonzero/nonfinite
denominator paths, rounding modes, inherited flags and positive trap controls.
Then replay the same masked/trapped physical fixtures, separately checking
amplitudes, host stability, actual precision path and trap completion. No
unchanged-path or physical-success claim follows from this source proof.

## Dilogarithm: the integer estimate changes the recurrence

The forced-QP site at ELF `0x2523cc3` is inside the MPFR `series` symbol, but
the instruction is binary64. The loaded numerator is 39.47841760435743,
consistent with inlined `series_terms` at `oneloop-dilog.rs:73–75`:

```text
ratio = 4*pi*pi / modulus
count = ceil((bits+6)*ln(2) / ln(ratio)) as usize + 1
```

`series:125–131` forms `v=u*u`, converts its components to binary64, computes
their hypotenuse, and selects zero terms if that modulus compares equal to
zero. Otherwise it uses the estimated count, capped by the coefficient table.
Lines 141–148 use `coefficients[count-1]` and the corresponding Horner steps
to compute the term added to the numerical answer. Thus this is a convergence
estimator **with a direct effect on the numerical recurrence**.

Under nearest rounding, a positive overflowing ratio becomes infinity. The
remaining expression then gives one term. A very large finite ratio instead
produces a positive quotient and at least two terms before the table cap.
A clamp or log-domain rewrite therefore cannot claim the old masked result.
Directed downward/toward-zero overflow may produce the largest finite value
instead of infinity, so an unconditional tiny-modulus-to-one guard is unsound.

There is a conditional proof worth recording, **not an implemented patch**:
if nearest rounding is explicitly verified, positive modulus words at most
`0x0030000000000000` represent values at most `2^-1020`. Since the numerator
exceeds 32, the exact ratio exceeds `2^1025`, guaranteeing a nearest-rounded
overflow to positive infinity. Substituting `ratio=INFINITY` only on that
integer-classified interval and retaining the original remaining expression
would preserve its one-term estimate. This conservative interval does not cover
every possible overflow input. It must not be used without the rounding
contract, and it would suppress the skipped overflow/inexact exceptions.

Keep the caller's signed-zero bypass: both zero signs currently select zero
terms there, whereas calling `series_terms` directly with zero follows a
different exceptional path. Preserve negative, nonfinite and all other input
bit patterns; do not introduce new NaN comparisons. DAZ/FTZ behavior, the actual
divisor, rounding mode and exception subtype are unobserved in the closed run.
No dilogarithm fix is proposed for implementation until that evidence or an
explicit, checked rounding contract exists. Independent scalar and amplitude
accuracy qualification would still be necessary.
